dissents.topic: Precedence: should custom_conda override auto-discovery, or be only a fallback?

positions.position: The UI label says 'use specified instead of finding from interpreter path' (override), but the code only consults custom_conda when find_conda() fails (fallback). The spec and the code disagree; one of them is wrong.
Treats the fallback shape as correct: 'try discovery, then try the user-configured path, then error with a pointer to the new preference.' Does not flag a UI/code mismatch.

dissents.topic: Where the (custom_conda=True, conda_path='') invariant should be enforced

positions.position: State the invariant and either enforce it at save-time in the confpage or handle the (True, '') state explicitly in kernelspec with a more specific error.
Enforce the postcondition inside kernelspec.argv itself — do not trust the preferences dialog to have validated; the resolution branch should verify the path exists and responds to --version.
Push the fix to the validator/UI: either return False on empty, or gate the checkbox on a non-empty path. Don't lie in the validator.
The two-key design is the root issue — collapse to one value (an optional path) so the invariant disappears rather than being enforced at multiple sites.
Either return a tri-state (None for unset) or document the sentinel explicitly; the function should not silently conflate unset with valid.
Absence and validity are different facts; push the empty-string semantics out to the caller — the validator should answer one question about one value.
Return False on empty; the validator is currently lying to the user, who sees 'valid' in preferences but a 'conda not found' error at kernel start.
Pick one of two contracts and state it: True-iff-working-conda (and move empty acceptance to the caller), or 'acceptable as a config value' (weaker postcondition, but documented).
Rename to `is_acceptable_conda_field` or push the empty-string case to the caller; a Maybe[Path] data shape would make this self-evident.
The empty-string case proves the postcondition is unstated; the predicate has no clear meaning until the spec is written.

dissents.topic: How to fix the loose substring match on --version output

positions.position: Parse the leading token of the version string and compare against a known set; state the invariant as 'output begins with one of {conda, mamba, micromamba}'.
Match the start of the version string or use a regex anchored to a version number.
Strip the cleverness: parse the first whitespace token, compare equality. Substring scanning is the wrong data shape.
Parse --version output into a value (name, version) and ask predicates of that value — identity-by-substring on free-form output is incidental complexity.
Use word-boundary or exact tool-name match; the weak postcondition is the real problem.
The substring approach is a fuzzy match dressed as validation; write a stated predicate before writing the code.

issues.description: filters='*.exe' breaks the file picker on Linux and macOS where conda binaries have no extension
issues.detail: Conda/mamba/micromamba on POSIX systems are extensionless; the *.exe filter hides every valid candidate in the browse dialog on the platforms where most conda users live. Either branch on sys.platform, use a platform-aware filter set, or drop the filter and rely on validate_conda as the gate. Multiple reviewers note this is the platform on which the feature most needs to work, since the feature exists specifically for non-standard install locations.

issues.description: validate_conda returns True for the empty string, conflating 'unset' with 'valid'
issues.detail: The early `if conda_executable == '': return True` overloads the predicate. Callers cannot distinguish 'no path provided' from 'path is a valid conda', the preferences UI shows 'valid' while kernelspec later errors that conda is not found, and absence/validity are mixed into one Boolean. Fixes proposed range from a tri-state return, to moving empty-string semantics to the caller, to gating the checkbox on non-empty path, to renaming the function to reflect the weaker contract.

issues.description: Substring match on --version output is too permissive and accepts non-conda binaries
issues.detail: `any(tool in out.decode().lower() for tool in ['micromamba', 'mamba', 'conda'])` will pass any binary whose --version output mentions any of those words anywhere — wrappers, help banners, tools named 'anaconda-something', even 'no mamba detected'. 'mamba' is also a substring of 'micromamba', making the iteration redundant. The proposed fix is to parse the leading token of the version string (or use an anchored regex) and compare for equality against a known set.

issues.description: validate_conda complects pure path-validation with side-effecting subprocess execution of a user-supplied binary
issues.detail: A function named 'validate' spawns a process against an arbitrary user-typed path with no timeout, swallows all exceptions, and has unstated frame and security implications. Identity checks, existence checks, executability checks, and a probe-by-execution are intertwined. Recommended decomposition: pure predicate over a value (path string), separated from a bounded act of running the binary to identify it, with a stated precondition for the input's trust level.

issues.description: Two config keys (custom_conda + conda_path) encode one fact, with the derivation rule re-implemented at the call site
issues.detail: The boolean toggle and the path string are read separately at every call site (notably kernelspec.argv), with the rule 'use the path only if the toggle is true' enforced by hand each time. This invites drift: custom_conda=True with empty conda_path, or custom_conda=False with a stale path. The simpler model is one value — an optional configured path — plus separate UI state if needed. The (True, '') invariant is currently enforced nowhere.

issues.description: Module boundary leak: kernelspec.py reaches across to main_interpreter config keys by untyped string
issues.detail: kernelspec.argv() reads `get_conf('conda_path', section='main_interpreter')` and `get_conf('custom_conda', section='main_interpreter')`, taking a dependency on another plugin's config schema via stringly-typed keys. The abstract 'conda executable resolution' responsibility is implemented partly in find_conda(), partly inline, with main_interpreter config as a back-channel. A single `resolve_conda_executable()` in spyder/utils/conda.py owning the contract 'return a path to a working conda exe, or None' would give callers one promise to depend on.

issues.description: create_browsefile / create_lineedit gain validate_callback and validate_reason with no documented contract
issues.detail: The two new keyword arguments are forwarded to create_lineedit, but the signature, invocation timing (keystroke? commit? focus-out?), expected return semantics, and meaning of validate_reason are nowhere stated. This is a contract widening on a widely-used widget factory; every future caller will write a validator with different assumptions, reproducing the empty-string ambiguity elsewhere. A docstring stating the callable's signature and the validator's precondition (must it accept empty string?) is required.

issues.description: kernelspec.argv fallback has no enforced postcondition that the chosen path is actually a working conda
issues.detail: The new branch trusts the preferences dialog to have validated, but config persistence is not gated by validate_conda; stored conda_path may be empty, stale, or pointing at a deleted file. State and enforce the block's postcondition here ('on exit, conda_exe is a path to an executable that responds to --version as conda/mamba/micromamba'), rather than depending on out-of-band validation.

issues.description: Custom-conda is consulted only on find_conda() failure, contradicting the UI text that says 'use instead of'
issues.detail: The user-facing checkbox/tooltip describes the custom path as an override of auto-detection, but the code uses it only as a fallback when find_conda() returns falsy. A user who explicitly sets a custom Conda because the auto-detected one is wrong will be silently ignored whenever auto-detection succeeds. Either flip the precedence to check custom_conda first, or change the UI text — the spec must match the code.

issues.description: The function name validate_conda overstates its guarantee given the actual predicate
issues.detail: The predicate is closer to 'looks like it could be a conda-family executable by name in --version output' than to 'this is a working conda'. Consider renaming to `looks_like_conda_executable` or `is_acceptable_conda_field`, or state the precise invariant in the docstring. Naming is part of the contract.

issues.description: run_program().communicate() in validate_conda has no timeout; a user-supplied path can hang the UI thread
issues.detail: Validation runs in the preferences dialog on the UI thread and will block indefinitely if the user points at a hung or interactive binary. Add a `communicate(timeout=...)` with TimeoutExpired handling that kills the process and returns False, and bound the lifecycle explicitly.

issues.description: out.decode() uses default encoding and silently fails on non-UTF-8 output
issues.detail: On systems with unusual locales or hostile binaries returning non-UTF-8 bytes, `.decode()` with no arguments raises UnicodeDecodeError, which the bare except swallows as False. Prefer `out.decode(errors='replace')` (or specify an explicit encoding) and document the choice; the silent-False failure mode masks real problems.

issues.description: validate_conda mixes early-return and a 'valid' flag, with inconsistent exception handling
issues.detail: Within one short function there are early-returns, a mutable flag set inside a try, and a return False in a bare-Exception catch. The reader must simulate the function to determine its return; the structured form is a sequence of guarded subchecks resolving to a single Boolean expression, or each gate returning explicitly with `return False` at the end. The bare except also hides distinct failure modes (decode errors, non-zero exit) behind one verdict.

issues.description: os.access(..., os.X_OK) is unreliable on POSIX under ACLs/NFS/setuid and essentially meaningless on Windows
issues.detail: The X_OK gate adds a code path that does nothing useful on Windows and can falsely reject on some POSIX configurations. The subsequent run_program() is the actual validator; the access check is redundant or harmful. Consider dropping it.

issues.description: No path normalization (strip, expanduser, quote-stripping) on user-entered conda_path
issues.detail: The textbox value is fed directly to os.path.isfile/os.access. A trailing space, surrounding quotes (common on Windows when pasting from file Properties), or `~` are not handled. A small `os.path.expanduser(path.strip().strip('"'))` removes a class of failures without algorithmic cleverness.

issues.description: edit.setFocus() added to the shared select_file helper changes behavior for every browsefile caller
issues.detail: `select_file` is shared infrastructure used by every browsefile widget in Spyder; adding `edit.setFocus()` silently widens its postcondition to 'the edit also has focus'. Whether intentional (perhaps to trigger validate_callback on focus-out) or accidental, the rationale is absent from the diff. If only the conda field needs it, wire it at the conda call site; if it is a general improvement, justify it as its own change.

issues.description: Three loosely related changes are folded into one PR (config plumbing, kernelspec fallback, widget focus tweak)
issues.detail: The edit.setFocus() change to the shared browsefile helper is unrelated to the custom-conda feature and affects every browsefile picker in Spyder. The config/kernelspec/validator work and the widget focus tweak should land as separate patches with separate justifications.

issues.description: Nested ternary in kernelspec.argv is harder to read than the data it represents
issues.detail: The replacement nests a ternary inside an assignment inside an `if not conda_exe`. The data is simple: 'custom path if enabled, else None'. Two lines — `custom_enabled = get_conf(...)` then `conda_exe = get_conf('conda_path', ...) if custom_enabled else None` — read cleaner and match the file's voice.

issues.description: No tests for validate_conda or the kernelspec fallback branch
issues.detail: validate_conda is a small function with clear branches (empty, missing file, non-executable, wrong tool, right tool) and is trivially testable; the kernelspec fallback (custom_conda enabled vs disabled, conda_path set vs empty) is the central behavior of the PR. Neither is exercised in this diff. The only correctness evidence offered is a screenshot. At minimum unit-test validate_conda's cases and a kernelspec test for the (custom_conda=True, conda_path='') error path.

issues.description: SPEC-MISSING on the new custom_conda/conda_path config pair and the invariant tying them together
issues.detail: Two new config keys are introduced with no documented invariant ('if custom_conda is True, conda_path must satisfy validate_conda; if False, conda_path is ignored'). The invariant is enforced nowhere — a user can toggle custom_conda on with an empty path and validate_conda('') returns True. Either enforce at save-time in the confpage or handle the (True, '') state explicitly in kernelspec with a clearer error.

synthesis.summary: All six reviewers converge on three strongest blockers: validate_conda returns True for the empty string (silently conflating 'unset' with 'valid'), the substring match on --version output is too permissive to be called validation, and the *.exe file filter breaks the picker on Linux/macOS where extensionless conda binaries are the norm — precisely the platforms where this feature is most needed. Beyond those, Hickey and Liskov call out a deeper modeling problem: two config keys encode one fact, the derivation rule is re-implemented at the kernelspec call site, and kernelspec.py reaches across module boundaries via untyped string keys instead of going through a single `resolve_conda_executable` abstraction. The strongest preserved disagreement is on precedence: Dijkstra reads the UI text as promising 'custom overrides auto-detection' but the code treats custom as a fallback only on find_conda() failure — Torvalds, by contrast, treats the fallback shape as the correct design. Secondary but recurring concerns include no subprocess timeout on a user-supplied binary executed in the UI thread, an unrelated `edit.setFocus()` change to a shared widget helper folded into a feature PR, and no tests for either validate_conda or the kernelspec fallback. Verdict spread runs from Torvalds's NEEDS-WORK to Dijkstra's REFUSED-as-written; nobody endorses merging as-is.
